[](https://star-history.com/#JetBrains/thinkrail&Date)

ThinkRail is the agentic IDE that gets better every time you use it — learning your project through
living specs today, and building its own capabilities tomorrow.

We built a rich interface around the `pi`
coding agent, isolated work into separate workspaces, and gave the agent durable project knowledge
through living specs and reusable skills. Next, we're adding full extension support, so ThinkRail can
create the tools it needs based on how you actually work.

**Website:** thinkrail.ai · **Blog:** thinkrail.ai/blog ·
**Discord:** thinkrail.ai/discord

⭐ If you find ThinkRail useful, give it a star — it helps others discover it.

 
  
             
  
 

 
   
   
 

*A `pi` session and the change it made, scoped to an isolated git-worktree workspace.*

## What you get

- **Isolated workspaces.** Open any git repo as a project and cut workspaces from it as `git worktree`s,
  each with its own branch and working directory. Agents work in parallel without touching your
  checkout; merge the good branch, delete the rest. You can also attach existing worktrees or explicitly
  work in the project folder itself. Finished and dormant workspaces settle onto a per-project shelf on
  their own — when their pull request merges or closes, or after a quiet week — and come back the moment
  you work in them. The topbar shows where the active branch stands against `origin` and its pull request,
  with the next step one click away: publish, push, or open a PR described from the plan, the commits,
  your PR template, or an agent-written draft. Once a GitHub PR is open it shows the CI checks and review
  decision, and lets you mark it ready, hand failing checks or a diverged branch to the agent, merge it
  with the repository's last-used method, reopen it, or delete the remote branch.
- **A real IDE around the agent.** A splittable workbench of Monaco editor tabs, a Files tree with live git
  change marks and a Changed view, terminals, and documents — all scoped to the active workspace. Leave
  anchored review comments on files and diffs and send them to a chat as structured context, or open the
  worktree in your installed IDE.

title: elayadesign/ai-design-skills
content:
# AI Design Skills

A growing collection of design skills for AI coding tools — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, and anything else that reads a markdown rules file.

Each skill is a self-contained folder. Install the ones you need.

---

## Skills

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `landing-page-design` | Builds a landing page from scratch — intake questions, page structure, conversion copy, plus a full visual system (type, spacing, radius, motion) |

More on the way. Upgrading an existing site instead of building new? That one lives in its own repo since it predates this collection.

---

## Install

Pick a skill from the table above, then swap ` ` below for its folder name.

 
  Claude Code  

```bash
mkdir -p .claude/skills
git clone https://github.com/elayadesign/ai-design-skills.git /tmp/ai-design-skills
cp -r /tmp/ai-design-skills/skills/  .claude/skills/
```

Then just ask, in plain language, for what that skill covers.
 

 
  Cursor  

```bash
mkdir -p .cursor/rules
curl -o .cursor/rules/ .md \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/elayadesign/ai-design-skills/main/skills/ /SKILL.md
```

Or paste the file into **Settings → Rules for AI**.
 

 
  Codex / Windsurf / other  

Copy the skill's `SKILL.md` into whatever your tool uses for project rules:

| Tool | Path |
|---|---|
| Codex | `AGENTS.md` |
| Windsurf | `.windsurfrules` |
| Cline | `.clinerules` |
| Generic | paste into your system prompt |
 

 
  Claude.ai (no terminal)  

Download the skill's `SKILL.md` and upload it to a Project, or attach it to a chat and say *"follow this."*
 

---

## Make it yours

Every skill's design values (fonts, colors, spacing, motion) live in one section near the bottom of its file. Fork this repo, edit that section, and the rest of the skill follows automatically.

---

## Credits

`landing-page-design` adapts content realism and motion ideas from Leonxlnx/taste-skill by Leon Lin, MIT licensed. Details are at the end of its SKILL.md.

---

## License

MIT. Use it, fork it, ship it, sell what you build with it. No attribution needed.

# Superpowers

Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.

## Table of Contents

## How it works

It starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent. As soon as it sees that you're building something, it *doesn't* just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do. 

Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest. 

After you've signed off on the design, your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow. It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It), and DRY. 

Next up, once you say "go", it launches a *subagent-driven-development* process, having agents work through each engineering task, inspecting and reviewing their work, and continuing forward. It's not uncommon for your agent to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together.

There's a bunch more to it, but that's the core of the system. And because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special. Your coding agent just has Superpowers.

If you're using Superpowers in enterprise and could benefit from commercial support, additional tooling, or managed spending, please don't hesitate to drop us a line at sales@primeradiant.com.

Installation differs by harness. If you use more than one, install Superpowers separately for each one.

Superpowers is available via the official Claude plugin marketplace


The Superpowers marketplace provides Superpowers and some other related plugins for Claude Code.


  ```bash
  /plugin install superpowers@superpowers-marketplace
  ```

content:

Macro is the all-in-one workspace for you and your team. It unifies email + messages + docs + tasks + agents + CRM into a single fast interface with shared team-level memory. Everything in your workspace is @linked and searchable so your team (and your agents) never have to switch tools. 
 
 

# Why Macro

We built Macro because we wanted a single operating system for our startup. There are many good software products, and we used them all — Slack, Linear, Notion, HubSpot, and Superhuman — but they don't work together as one system. As we scaled our last venture to ~20 people things started to break: every team got their own tools and the company was held together by MCP and Zapier. The company was not computable. It was chaotic.

Macro is a complete redesign of work software from the ground up as a single system.

Designed by us in NYC and Toronto, dogfooded by our team of ~15 for two years. Built in SolidJS and Rust for speed and reliability. We're focused on building something that any small company or team at a larger company can use as their "operating system".

 

# Features

Macro is composed of 'blocks' designed to be modular, extensible, and work together like Lego. For each block, we studied the best prior art and tried to make it even better.

Each surface is purpose-built for its job rather than composed from a generic block primitive — but every one of them shares the same backend; cross-references between a doc and a task, or a channel message and an email, are natively stored as a **bidirectional graph**.

| Block         | Docs                                                      | What it does                                                                  |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Email         | Docs →       | Multi-account unified inbox, keyboard shortcuts, and shared inboxes. Gmail.   |
| Messages      | Docs →    | Channels and direct messages designed for focused technical discussions.      |
| Tasks         | Docs →       | Linear-inspired tasks, tightly integrated with channels, email, and agents.   |
| Docs          | Docs →        | Real-time collaborative, markdown-native docs built on CRDTs, with @mentions. |
| Canvas        | Docs →      | 2D board with embedded @links to tasks, files, and emails.                    |
| Agents        | Docs →      | Unified, team-level memory. Can take action on your behalf.                   |
| Calls         | Docs →       | Recorded, transcribed, and logged to team memory for agents.                  |
| File storage  | Docs →     | Auto-imported from email and channels, fully searchable.                      |

# Hallmark

**A design skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode that refuses to look AI-generated.**

usehallmark.com  ·  fifty themes  ·  custom on request  ·  redesign and audit by name

Made by Together AI.

 
   
 

Hallmark holds a hard floor and then gets out of the way. It deals three themes from a catalog of fifty materials, builds the page around what the visitor came to do, and lints the result in a real browser against the tells that read as machine-made: the eyebrow above every heading, tracked-capital labels, one coloured word in a headline, a page of empty frames or nothing but photographs, a hero that misses its screen, an email sign-up at the end of every page, a form that says thanks without sending anything. A fresh-context reviewer gets the last word.

The gates come in tiers. The **Floor** never ships (contrast, focus, reduced motion, invented facts, a broken phone layout). **Reflex** gates are the defaults a model falls into; a build with a reason may overrule one on the record. **Finish** checks are craft detail that never blocks a ship.

## New in v2

- **Fifty themes.** Each is a material (paper, type, colour, surfaces, its own components and texture) with a picture of a finished page, and the build lays out its own page in it.
- **Built from the job.** A booking page books, a shop sells, a newsletter subscribes: the action sits where the category puts it, and the page ends on it.
- **Custom.** Ask for a custom page and Hallmark designs from your prompt alone, under the same rules and checks.
- **Your real product.** Point it at a URL, a dev server or an app and it captures the screenshots itself.
- **Real photographs.** 755 openly licensed photos, picked per subject and credited on the page.
- **Redesign and audit.** `/hallmark redesign  ` rebuilds a page and keeps its content and wiring; `/hallmark audit  ` only reports.

## Themes

 
   
         
         
         
         
         
   
   
      Dusk   Closewise, bank reconciliation  
      Cobalt   Relay, a webhook API  
      Studio   Field Office, an identity studio  
      Atelier   Maison Orla, a fragrance atelier  
      Ribbon   Lull, a sleep sounds app  
   
   
         
         
         
         
         
   
   
      Furrow   Fieldbook, farm records  
      Dose   Tandem, a family medication app  
      Refract   Bellwater Lido, an outdoor pool  
      Vantage   Swath, construction site scans  
      Hedgerow   Five Mile Gin, a distillery  
   
 

Ten of the fifty. A theme is a material, not a plan: it never says what a page contains or in what order, so two prompts in one theme make two different pages. Each is one file of at most 8 KB in `references/themes/` with a picture beside it; a build reads exactly one. See them all at usehallmark.com.

content:
# Impeccable

The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with `polish` and `bolder`, review with `critique` and `audit`, and catch AI slop before it ships.

From your project root:

```bash
npx impeccable install
```

Reload your coding tool, then run `/impeccable init` in your agent (`$impeccable init` on Codex).

Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at impeccable.style/docs.

| Without Impeccable | With Impeccable |
|---|---|
|  |  |

Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water.

For a full project, see the Neo Mirai case study: a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page.

## Why

Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects.

- **Words for what you want.** "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. `/impeccable bolder the pricing cards` loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target.
- **A reviewer.** `critique` scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. `audit` checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish).
- **A slop detector.** 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key.

Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see Build something new for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component:

```
/impeccable critique the pricing cards
```

## How it works

Run `/impeccable init` once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes `PRODUCT.md`. Every later command reads it. Run `/impeccable document` to capture your existing visual system in `DESIGN.md`, so changes stay on-brand. More on context files.

Then name a command and a target:

```
/impeccable critique the onboarding flow
/impeccable quieter the landing page
/impeccable polish settings
/impeccable harden checkout
```

Or just describe what you want: `/impeccable redo this hero section`. Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with `/impeccable pin audit` to get `/audit` as its own shortcut.

English  ·  简体中文 
 

 
     
     
 

 
    Download Cindy    ·   Website   ·   Build with us   ·   Get help 
 

Cindy is an **open-source AI agent, ready out of the box and yours to shape**.
Connect your computers and phone, bring the models and subscriptions you already
use, and build a companion that knows how you like to work.

## All your devices. One Cindy.

Your work computer, home desktop, laptop and phone belong together.

- **Pick up the same work.** Open a session from another device, continue the
  conversation, and access its files without copying everything into a new chat.
- **Share more than a screen.** Use model providers configured on another
  computer — including supported subscriptions, API providers and local models.
- **Reach your whole desktop.** Built-in remote desktop on your phone lets you
  open apps, type and operate a connected computer when a chat isn't enough.

Your computer becomes your server: **no server rental or self-hosting setup**.

 
 How connections and data work 

For remote access to your computers, keep them online, sign in with the same
account and enable the relevant permissions. Model sharing requires allowing
remote access to that provider; remote desktop also needs its own permissions.
Project files stay on their computer — remote access is not whole-disk sync.
Cloud companions sync their conversations, memory, skills and shared attachments
through Cindy's services; model providers process the requests sent to them.
Provider and service billing still apply.

 

## Keep your favorite agents. Get a better way to work.

Already using Claude Code or Codex? Cindy brings them together with **Pi**,
then adds a shared interface, multi-device access, tools and a companion of
your own.

| Harness | What it brings |
| --- | --- |
| **Claude Code** | Claude Code's agent workflow, with Cindy's interface and connected tools. |
| **Codex** | Codex's coding workflow, available alongside your other agents. |
| **Pi** | A lean, open-source, extensible agent with support for multiple model providers. |

Choose a supported harness and model combination, and change it as the work
evolves. Your session stays in Cindy; switching harnesses hands off or rebuilds
the engine context rather than making their internal states identical.

**One agent not enough? Let her lead a team.** Use different agents for planning,
parallel implementation and independent review, with a shared goal and clear
acceptance criteria.

## Real work, in your actual tools

Work with your files, browser and apps. Ask for a change, inspect what happened,
and keep working from the result. Answers can include **charts, interactive
controls and rich HTML**, not just a wall of text.

Build a recurring routine with **automations**, or hand over work through
connected chat channels such as Slack and Telegram. Connect more tools through
**Skills, plugins and MCP**.

## Ready from day one. Yours to shape over time.
